scope: Author-run scripted comparison on the public Portaldot V3 testnet nodes. N = 1 run per mode. No human participant, no external maintainer, no adoption or willingness-to-pay evidence. Owner, reviewer and operator are project-controlled accounts. Case-level findings only.

protocol.question: May the pUSD entry { chainId 420420777, 0x00001e61...10000, pUSD, Portaldot USD (test), 6 decimals, asset 7777 } be enabled in the catalog right now?

baseline.name: CI script + explorer + approval record
baseline.reads: JSON-RPC eth_call at the EVM hash of the finalized block (ethers for ABI), polkadot-js storage and blocks at the native hash; one connection per run, sequential reads
baseline.record: the maintainer keeps the approved report hash, the revision and the remark.store extrinsic and block hash (what the explorer shows)
baseline.output: maintainer-ci-script.result.v1: configuration echo, checkpoint, five checks with observed values, problem labels, decision, exit code

revivecheck.name: ReviveCheck policy evaluation and catalog entry comparison
revivecheck.implementation: lib/policy.js evaluateBinding; examples/token-catalog/lib/catalog.js buildCatalog (approvedEntry, compareEntry); live inputs from lib/service.js collectPolicyInputs
revivecheck.invocation: library calls in-process, the same calls catalog.js acceptance makes; the CLI was not spawned so both arms share one process and one timing tap
revivecheck.output: catalog.json and evaluations/<token>.json as the CLI writes them, bundled

checks.name: entry-vs-chain
checks.expected: every entry field equals the chain through both interfaces
checks.revivecheck: approvedEntry requires a passed token.listing check that confirmed chainId, address, symbol, name and decimals through both interfaces at the report checkpoint; compareEntry requires the configured entry to equal that approved entry field by field (entry-mismatch:<field> otherwise); target.subject ties the report to the policy subject

checks.name: trusted-approval
checks.expected: the current revision carries the recorded report hash and the trusted reviewer approved it
checks.revivecheck: registry.read, registry.provenance, registry.domain, registry.fresh, registry.interfaces, registry.release, registry.owner, registry.label, registry.revision (exact report hash and revision), registry.approvals (trusted set, threshold, no request for changes)

checks.name: listing-entry
checks.expected: listed on the recorded release, report hash and reviewer
checks.revivecheck: consumer.read, consumer.provenance, consumer.domain, consumer.fresh, consumer.identity, consumer.registry, consumer.version-known, consumer.version, consumer.interfaces, consumer.listed, consumer.entry (release, exact report hash, a trusted reviewer)

checks.name: stored-report
checks.expected: the stored report is in a canonical finalized block and its canonical SHA-256 is the recorded hash
checks.revivecheck: storage.read (retrieved from a canonical finalized block, Remark.Stored event matches publisher and content hash, SHA-256 verifies), storage.report (it is the bound report)

checks.name: age-runtime
checks.expected: the report is within the maximum age and pinned the runtime the chain runs now
checks.revivecheck: evidence.age, runtime.report, observation.present, observation.fresh, observation.network, runtime.current

reviveCheckOnly: evidence.integrity (binding hash and report hash verify under this exact policy)
interface agreement for registry and consumer reads
consumer identity and version at the listing checkpoint
a documented reason vocabulary with the status each reason forces and a next action
baselineOnly: C1 re-reads the asset metadata at the evaluation checkpoint in live mode; ReviveCheck relies on the sealed report's token.listing check at the report checkpoint, bounded by evidence.age
protocol.deterministicInputs: Both arms consume the same captured inputs file (revivecheck.token-catalog-inputs.v1). The baseline replays registry.views.*.evm and listing.views.*.evm as its eth_call results, the observation as its finalized checkpoint and runtime, and evidence.run as the report it would decode from the block. No separate asset read was captured, so its C1 chain values come from the stored report's raw token.listing evidence (native field values and raw ERC-20 return data, decoded by the script) at the report checkpoint, which is also the checkpoint ReviveCheck's approvedEntry relies on. Both arms evaluate at the capture's recorded time.
protocol.liveInputs: Each arm opens its own connection and reads a fresh finalized checkpoint; the checkpoints are recorded per arm and may differ by a block or more. The baseline reads sequentially; collectPolicyInputs reads observation, registry and listing in parallel and then the stored report.
protocol.timing: wallMs: the arm's wall clock including its connection handshake and teardown. networkWaitMs: the union of intervals during which at least one network call was in flight (fetch for JSON-RPC, WsProvider.send and connect for the native node). computeMs = wallMs - networkWaitMs. networkCallSumMs: the sum of individual call durations; it exceeds networkWaitMs when calls overlap. connectMs: the WebSocket handshake. Every call is listed in callLog.
protocol.counterbalancing: Live arm order alternates per scenario and is recorded. Scripts have no learning effect; the alternation only balances connection warm-up and node load.
protocol.correctness: correct: the decision equals the predefined expectation; false-enable: enabled when the expectation was refuse; false-refusal: refused when the expectation was enable; incomplete: the arm threw and produced no decision.
protocol.operatorActions: Distinct commands a person runs plus values a person must derive by hand (not copy from a record) to obtain one repeat decision for one scenario, once the arm is set up. Setup effort is counted separately under installation.
protocol.assistance: Requests for help and corrections by a person during the task.
protocol.writes: none: no wallet is loaded and nothing is signed; all chain access is read-only

installation.note: First-time effort, measured once and separately from repeat decisions. Field counts stand in for the time to write a configuration; the time a person needs to read documentation, type, or understand a field was not measured.

freshClone.method: git clone --local of this repository into an empty temporary directory outside the repository, then `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund` in the clone; each step timed by wall clock in a Node wrapper (performance.now). The local npm cache was warm, so package tarballs were not downloaded. The clone was deleted afterwards.
freshClone.humanTime: not measured: no person read documentation or typed during this measurement

freshClone.method: The same fresh clone (commit 4dfb1e36000d09ff14a95855ee6bd8080c273542) with node_modules removed, then `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund --cache <empty directory>` so every package tarball was downloaded; timed by wall clock in a Node wrapper (performance.now). Residential network, Apple Silicon laptop. The clone and the cache directory were deleted afterwards.
freshClone.humanTime: not measured: no person read documentation or typed during this measurement

steps: git clone and npm ci (measured above)
write the catalog configuration with its policy
obtain the sealed report (check_release or an existing published report) and store it on-chain, or reference the stored one
bind the exact report once per approved revision: catalog.js bind with six arguments
run catalog.js acceptance for every later decision
reviveCheckSetup.valuesCopiedNotDerived: the release ID, report hash, extrinsic hash and block hash are copied from receipts or read_registry output; none is computed by hand

steps: write the script (its facts are listed under knowledge)
look up the stored report extrinsic hash and block hash in the explorer or the publishing receipt
record the approved report hash and revision
run the script for every decision
knowledge: The ERC-20 precompile address scheme of native assets on Portaldot V3 (u32 big-endian id, 12 zero bytes, 00010000), verified for spec 3002 only.
Native and EVM block hashes differ; ReviveApi.ethBlockHash maps the finalized native block to the EVM block tag for eth_call.
The runtime types bundle for spec 3002 (NativeOrWithId / TAssetConversion), without which block decoding fails.
The ReleaseRegistry ABI (releaseOf, decisionOf) and the release ID scheme keccak256(abi.encode(owner, bytes32(label))).
The VerifiedTokenList ABI (isListed, entryOf) and that an entry names a release, a report hash and a reviewer.
Where the report bytes are: the remark.store extrinsic hash and block hash, taken from the explorer or the publishing receipt.
The canonical JSON form that the report hash is computed over (sorted keys, undefined dropped, evidenceHash excluded).
Which report fields date it (completedAt) and pin its runtime (network.specName/specVersion).
The ERC-20 metadata ABI (symbol, name, decimals) and how to decode the returned strings and uint8.
Which reviewer counts as trusted, and that the release owner approving its own release does not.
dependencies: the project connection helper lib/chain.js connectNative for the spec-3002 types bundle
